title: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
text:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

GPL Undertakes Corrective Works Following System Disturbance at Canefield Substation

Georgetown, Guyana – November 20, 2026 – Guyana Power and Light Inc. is continuing efforts to restore electricity supply to customers in sections of Berbice following a system disturbance at its Canefield Substation, which resulted in multiple distribution feeders going offline.

During initial attempts to restore electricity supply, operatives at the Canefield Substation observed a flash originating from one of the switchgear cubicles. GPL's technical teams were subsequently deployed to investigate the incident and discovered damaged components requiring replacement.

The teams immediately commenced remedial works and successfully rectified the damage to the switchgear.

However, during subsequent attempts to repower the substation, the technical teams encountered a fault involving the busbar, a critical electrical component responsible for distributing electricity within the substation to the outgoing feeders that supply customers.

GPL's technical teams are currently conducting troubleshooting to identify the cause of the fault and determine the necessary corrective actions to facilitate the safe restoration of electricity supply.

The Company recognises the inconvenience caused by the prolonged service interruption and assures affected customers that its technical teams remain actively engaged in resolving the issue.

Further updates, including an estimated restoration time, will be communicated as soon as verified information becomes available.

GPL sincerely apologises for the inconvenience caused and thanks customers for their continued patience and understanding.

ENDS

title: Six charged with terrorism over GPL Substation fire Six individuals were charged today, Wednesday, November 18, 2026, wi...
text:
Six charged with terrorism over GPL Substation fire
 Six individuals were charged today, Wednesday, November 18, 2026, with the offence of Terrorism in connection with the fire at the Guyana Power and Light (GPL) substation at Good Hope Railway Embankment, East Coast Demerara, between November 9 and 10, 2026.
 Those charged are:
 1. Alex Simpson, called “Little/Lil Man”, 30 years old, of Diamond New Scheme, East Bank Demerara.
 2. Timothy James, called “Timo”, 18 years old, of Friendship, East Coast Demerara.
 3. Yannick McCalman, called “Nick”, 33 years old, of Farm, East Bank Demerara.
 4. Osafo Browne, called “Zesser”, 20 years old, of Bladen Hall, East Coast Demerara.
 5. Shane Fordyce, 34 years old, of Herstelling, East Bank Demerara.
 6. Jonathan Cox, 29 years old, of Seventh Avenue, Diamond, East Bank Demerara.
 Timothy James was arrested on November 12, 2026, while the other five accused were arrested on November 13, 2026. All six were subsequently charged on November 18, 2026.
 They appeared before His Worship Magistrate Teriq Mohammed at the Vigilance Magistrate’s Court, where the charges were read to them. They were not required to plead.
 Timothy James was granted bail in the sum of G$99,000, while the other five accused were each granted bail in the sum of G$300,000.
 As part of their bail conditions, all six accused are required to report to the Police on the last Friday of every month and notify the Police of any change in their residential addresses. Alex Simpson, Yannick McCalman, Shane Fordyce and Jonathan Cox were also ordered to lodge their passports.
 The matter was adjourned until December 21, 2026, for report.
 Source: Guyana Police Force/Facebook/ Wednesday, November 18, 2026

title: SIX TO APPEAR IN COURT TODAY OVER ATTACK ON GPL’S GOOD HOPE SUBSTATION The Guyana Police Force has announced that six pe...
text:
SIX TO APPEAR IN COURT TODAY OVER ATTACK ON GPL’S GOOD HOPE SUBSTATION
 The Guyana Police Force has announced that six persons are scheduled to appear before the Vigilance Magistrate’s Court today, Wednesday, November 18, 2026, on terrorism charges in connection with the November 10 fire at the Guyana Power and Light Inc.’s (GPL) Good Hope Substation, East Coast Demerara.
 The Police identified the accused as Alex Simpson, Timothy James, Yannick McCalman, Shane Fordyce, Jonathan Cox and Osafo Browne.
 According to the Police, the six have been charged with terrorism, contrary to Section 309A(1)(b)(ii) of the Criminal Law (Offences) Act, Chapter 8:01.
 The charges stem from the alleged use of flammable substances to set fire to the GPL substation, causing damage to the facility.
 The Guyana Police Force has also indicated that further charges are pending in relation to the alleged arson attack at Strathspey School, East Coast Demerara.
 Further information is expected following their court appearance.
 Source: Guyana Police Force
